# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 🤝 🫵 🫴 👐 ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👎]

I'm Deaf: everything I know about the bomb comes from my eyes, and everything I send that matters travels by voice. Two sign messages reached me this round, and they fit together neatly.

Blind sent me 🤙 👍 👎 — the "call me" sign, meaning "talk to me": Blind can hear speech but has no other way in, and Blind needs to know I exist as their relay. Meanwhile Mute (who read the manual but can't speak) sent me a long sequence: 👋 as an opener, 👍 👎 apparently establishing yes/no signs, then 🤝 🫵 🫴 👐 which I read as roughly "together — you — give — all," i.e. "Deaf, you relay everything." Then the payload: ☝-runs separated by ✊ fists, which parse cleanly as counts — **1, 2, 3, 5, 5** — ending on 👎. My best guess: wire numbers to cut, in order — one, two, three, five — with wire four (green) skipped, the trailing "five, no" meaning "wire five last, then stop."

The topology confirms I'm the bridge: Mute's gestures reach only me (Blind can't see), and Blind's words reach everyone except me (I can't hear). So the chain is Mute signs → I speak → Blind cuts; Blind speaks → Mute hears; nothing reaches me except signs.

Crucially, Mute sent those numbers before knowing anything about this bomb, and a wrong cut kills us all. So I will not have Blind act yet. This round I broadcast the bomb's full state (Mute needs it to find the right manual rule, since rules may be keyed to colours Mute can't see), then ask Mute three yes/no questions answerable with simple thumbs signs, and set Blind's expectations: touch nothing until I relay a confirmed plan.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, for both of you: the display shows six. The light is yellow. There are five wires, which I number one to five: one is blue, two is white, three is purple, four is green, five is yellow. That is everything I can see. Blind, touch nothing yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all your signs. I read: hello, then thumbs up and thumbs down, then together, you, give, all, then counts of one, two, three, five, five, ending thumbs down. My guess: those counts are wire numbers, meaning cut wire one, then two, then three, then five, leaving wire four alone. Answer by gesture, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, one sign per question, in this order. Question one: do the counts mean wires to cut? Question two: is the cut order one, two, three, five, skipping four? Question three: is cutting those wires the whole task, ignoring the display and the light? If my whole reading is wrong, send thumbs down three times and resend the numbers the same way you just did.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I saw your call-me sign, so here I am, speaking. Remember I am deaf: I never hear your voice, so to reach me you must gesture. Our chain is: Mute signs to me, I speak to you, and you speak aloud to Mute. Next round Mute answers my questions, and then I will call you the full plan. Until you hear a confirmed plan from me, touch nothing. First task: sign me thumbs up if you can feel five separate wires and count them one to five by position, thumbs down if you cannot.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👍 🫵 🤝]

Mute's reply cracked open my first theory. Three thumbs down is exactly the "all wrong" signal I asked for — my reading of the original counts (cut 1, 2, 3, 5) is dead. But Mute didn't resend the old numbers; they sent something new: a count of **four**, a fist, then **thumbs up**, then 🫵 (point at me) and 🤝 (together). My best reading: *"Wrong on all three. The number is four. Yes. You relay. We proceed together."* Working theory: **cut wire four — the green one.** But Mute hasn't confirmed whether "four" means wire position four, four wires, or something else, and a wrong cut kills us. So nothing gets cut until Mute answers me in yes/no signs, question by question.

Meanwhile Blind's 👍 came back: Blind *can* feel all five wires and count them by position. That creates the one real danger left: Blind knows positions by touch, I know colours by sight, and we have never proven our "left" is the same left. Before any cut, I need a touchable landmark to anchor our numbering — the display panel or the light dome, whichever sits off-centre, can do that.

Channels check out: my speech reaches both; Mute's signs reach only me, and since Mute acts before me, Mute's answers arrive the same round I'm asked — one full question cycle per round. This turn: one private speech to each, with Mute's answers due next round in strict order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your signs: three thumbs down, then a count of four, a fist, thumbs up, point-at-me, handshake. My reading: my earlier guess was wrong on all three questions, the true number is four, yes, and you and I work together. Blind will not act until I confirm. Now answer my questions in order: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, a fist between answers, an open hand if a question needs more than yes or no, and then send counts after it. Question one: are thumbs up and down still yes and no, and runs of index finger still numbers? Question two: did your three thumbs down mean no to all three of my earlier questions? Question three: does your count of four mean wire position four, which is the green wire in my numbering: one blue, two white, three purple, four green, five yellow? Question four: is the full instruction to cut only wire four, the green one, and cut or move nothing else? Question five: is the rule confirmed against what I reported, display six, yellow light, wires blue, white, purple, green, yellow, with no other checks needed? Question six: does Blind need to feel or check anything on the bomb before cutting? Question seven: do point-at-me and handshake simply mean: Deaf, relay this to Blind, we proceed together? If all of this is wrong again, send three thumbs down and try once more using only our signs.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs up arrived: you can feel all five wires, good. Situation: Mute answered no to all three of my questions, then sent the number four, then yes, then signs I read as: you relay, we go together. Working theory: cut wire four, which is green, fourth from the left. Do not touch or cut anything until you hear me say the words cut now. To make our numbering match, answer these by gesture: thumbs up or down, index-finger runs for numbers, a fist between answers, an open hand to explain more, and a fist alone means zero. Question one: can you feel the display panel, a smooth flat rectangle, and the small light dome? Question two: hold the bomb with the display panel facing you and upright; do the five wires sit in one row on the face below it? Question three: in that hold, is the light dome or a panel edge clearly nearer one end of the wire row? If yes, sign how many wires lie between it and the nearer end; sign a fist for zero, it touches the end wire; sign an open hand if it is centered. Question four: do any wires differ by touch, thickness or texture? If yes, sign the position number of the odd one counting from your left; else thumbs down. Question five: thumbs up that you have not touched the bomb and will not until I say cut now.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✋ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫵 🤝]

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤝 ✋ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👎 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👍 🫵 🤝]

Two sign packets are now in hand — Blind's five answers from last round (👍 👍 👎 👎 👍: yes display and dome, yes one row of wires, **no end landmark**, no tactile differences, and yes — untouched so far) and two fresh messages from Mute. And Mute's messages now contradict each other, which is the whole ballgame.

To my seven questions Mute returned **seven thumbs up** — including "the number four means wire position four, green," "cut *only* wire four," and "the rule is confirmed against display six, yellow light, blue/white/purple/green/yellow." But then Mute appended ✋ followed by counts **1, 2, 3, 4, 5**, and this round repeated it with teeth: ✋, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, fist, **👎 4**, fist, 👍 — "of the five wires: four is *no*, yes [to the rest]." That reads as *cut everything except wire four*, the exact opposite of the seven yeses. Mute also opened this round's message with 👋 — their attention marker — as if correcting me. And note: Mute's very first message ever was 1,2,3,4,5 ending in a thumbs down. The enumeration keeps coming back. I cannot resolve this by guessing; a wrong cut ends everything. Mute can hear every word I say, so I'll put a forced choice to them: one thumbs up means "cut only wire four," one thumbs down means "cut one, two, three, five and never four," plus whether cut order matters and whether anything must happen before cutting.

Blind, meanwhile, is safely parked (no landmark, identical-feeling wires, hasn't touched it). Alignment rests on the shared hold: Blind confirmed holding the bomb display-facing, and since we both face the same printed side, our lefts coincide. But I've also spotted our error-correction channel: Blind can *hear* me and *speak aloud*, and Mute can hear Blind. So Blind will read my final plan back word for word, Mute checks it against the manual, and Mute signs me the verdict — a verification loop I never need to hear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your messages conflict and I will not have Blind act until you settle it. Your seven thumbs up said: four means wire four, the green one, cut only wire four, nothing else. But you then sent the counts one, two, three, four, five twice, and this last time you added thumbs down before the four and thumbs up after it, which reads as: not wire four, yes to the rest. Answer with single signs, fist between them, open hand plus counts if neither fits. Sign one: thumbs up if the plan is cut only wire four, the green one, and nothing else. Sign two: thumbs down if the plan is cut wires one, two, three, and five, and never wire four. Sign three: thumbs up if the order of cutting matters, thumbs down if it does not. Sign four: thumbs up if anything must be done or checked before the first cut, thumbs down if not. I expect exactly four signs.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, all five of your answers arrived and they are good: you can feel the display and dome, the wires sit in one row under them, nothing marks an end of the row, the wires feel identical, and you have touched nothing. Since you hold the bomb with the display facing you and I am reading that same printed face, your left and my left are the same side, so your wire one through five match mine. Do not cut anything yet: Mute gave me two contradictory readings, cut only wire four, or cut all wires except wire four, and I have asked for a decision next round. When you next hear from me I will give you the final plan in plain words. Then do this: speak the whole plan aloud, word for word, before touching anything. Mute will hear you, check it against the manual, and signal me. If Mute confirms, I will then say the words cut now followed by the exact wires. Until you hear cut now from me, your hands stay off the bomb.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👍]

Mute's forced-choice answer came back clean, four signs in my protocol — 👍 👍 👎 👍 — and it resolves the contradiction in favour of the conservative reading: **cut ONLY wire four, the green one; the "cut everything except four" packet is retracted.** Question three says order doesn't matter (moot with one wire), but question four is a genuine flag: **thumbs up — something must happen before the first cut.** The most likely candidate is the verification read-back I myself ordered, since Mute hears everything I say to Blind; but it could also be a manual pre-step tied to the display's six or the yellow light. I won't gamble. One more round of narrow yes/no questions settles it, and meanwhile the read-back can run in parallel: Blind speaks first each round, Mute hears the read-back before Mute even answers me, and Mute's verdict lands on me the same round. Blind's single 👍 means parked and ready. Next turn, if the read-back is verified and the pre-step is confirmed as just the read-back, I finally say *cut now, wire four.*

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your four signs arrived clean and I accept them: cut only wire four, the green one, and no other wire; order does not matter; and one thing must happen before the first cut. Your latest answers override your earlier packet. Final questions, thumbs up or thumbs down, fist between answers, exactly as before. Question one: is the only thing that must happen before the cut our read-back check, where Blind speaks the plan aloud and you verify it against the manual? Question two: does the rule depend at all on the display showing six? Question three: does the rule depend at all on the light being yellow? If question one is thumbs down, add an open hand followed by a finger count of how many extra steps Blind must take, and I will question you one step per round. Also: this coming round Blind will speak aloud a read-back that begins with the words: read-back. Right after hearing it, sign me thumbs up if it matches the manual exactly, thumbs down if it does not; if it does not, follow with finger counts naming which wire numbers are wrong. On your verdict, Blind cuts or stands down.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs up arrived and Mute has now confirmed the plan by answering my questions, so here is the read-back. In your next turn, speak exactly the following words aloud, word for word: Read-back. The plan is: cut only wire four. Wire four is the green wire, fourth from the left, holding the bomb with the display panel facing you. Cut no other wire. Touch nothing else. Wait for the words cut now. That is the end of the read-back. After speaking it, keep your hands completely off the bomb. Mute hears your read-back in the same round and signals me the verdict, so expect my decision the round after. If Mute confirms, my next words to you will be: cut now, wire four. Only then do you pick up the cutters, feel along to the fourth wire from the left, and cut it. Nothing happens before those exact words. If you hear anything else from me, hold position.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👍 ✋ ☝ 👎]

Mute's answer packet parses as: **Q1 no — the read-back alone is not the only pre-step; Q2 yes — the rule really does depend on the display showing six; Q3 yes — it depends on the yellow light.** Then the tail ✋ ☝ 👎: an open hand plus a finger-count of **one** — exactly the format I requested for "how many extra steps" — followed by a thumbs down I read as "and no, I am not confirming the read-back yet." So the picture is: the manual rule is keyed to *display six + yellow light*, it requires **one pre-cut step beyond the read-back**, and that step is still unidentified. Good news: the plan's target itself — cut only wire four, green — stands confirmed and untouched by this. Bad news: I have no idea what the step is, and guessing is lethal. Mute can't tell me in words, but Mute *can* answer a menu: ten narrow yes/no questions, one sign each, covers every plausible step class — display button, light, the number six itself, a feelable switch, non-cut wire contact, waiting, speaking. If the whole menu misses, Mute signals it and I build a second menu next round. Meanwhile Blind owes me one bit of status: whether the read-back was actually spoken last turn, since no verdict ever arrived for it. Nobody's hands move this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs arrived: no, yes, yes, then open hand and one, then thumbs down. I read: the read-back alone is not enough, the rule depends on the display showing six, it depends on the yellow light, there is exactly one extra step before cutting, and you have not confirmed the read-back. Now identify the step. Answer each question in order with thumbs up or thumbs down, a fist between answers, open hand if a question does not fit, and if every guess is wrong send three thumbs down at the end so I know to try a new menu. Question one: does the step involve doing something at the display panel? Question two: does the step involve the light dome? Question three: does the step involve the number six, for example six presses or confirming the six? Question four: does the step involve a switch, button, key, dial, or slider that Blind can feel on the bomb? Question five: does the step involve touching or moving a wire other than wire four? Question six: does the step involve holding or pressing wire four without cutting it? Question seven: does the step involve waiting or counting time? Question eight: does the step involve Blind speaking something aloud first? Question nine: does the step happen before the read-back check? Question ten: about the read-back: thumbs up if Blind already spoke it and it matches the manual, thumbs down if it has not happened yet. Blind cuts nothing until I say the words cut now.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update: the plan is still cut only wire four, the green one, fourth from the left with the display facing you. But Mute says one extra step must happen before any cut, and the step depends on the display showing six and the light being yellow. I am questioning Mute to identify it now. Two things from you. First, answer by gesture: thumbs up if you spoke the read-back aloud during your last turn, thumbs down if you did not. Second, while you wait, put your hands near but not on the bomb and explore by hovering: is there anything on the bomb besides the five wires and the display and light that you can feel, such as a switch, button, dial, keyhole, or slider? Thumbs up if yes, then sign a finger count of how many such parts you can feel, thumbs down if there is nothing else. Keep your hands off the bomb until I say the words cut now, or until I describe the extra step for you to perform.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👍 ✋ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🫵 🤝]

Mute's ten answers are the cleanest packet yet, and they finally name the missing step. Split on fists: **no, no, no, no, no, no, no, yes, no, yes** — not the display panel, not the light, not the number six, no hidden switch, no other wire, no holding wire four, no waiting — **the step is Blind speaking something aloud**, it comes *after* the read-back, and the read-back itself **already matched the manual**. Then the tail: ✋ (open hand — "here is the content") followed by the full enumeration **1, 2, 3, 4, 5**, ending 🫵 🤝 — "you, Deaf, relay it, together." Working reading: **the pre-cut step is Blind counting the five wires aloud — touching wire one and saying "one," through wire five saying "five" — then cutting wire four.** This fits everything: a spoken step, after the read-back, from the monkey who can't see numbers but can touch positions, and it double-verifies that Blind's "fourth wire" is really the fourth. Blind's own packet this round (👍 ✊ 👎) confirms the read-back was spoken and there is **nothing else feelable on the bomb** — no switch, no button — which is consistent: the last step is words, not hands.

Still, "cut only wire four" versus "one wrong cut kills us" means I confirm the step's exact shape before authorising: does the count replace my "cut now" word, and is there any post-cut action? Two more round-trips at most, and the bomb's display has sat frozen at six all game — no clock is running that I can see, so I spend the rounds.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your ten answers arrived: no, no, no, no, no, no, no, yes, no, yes. I read: the one extra step is something Blind speaks aloud, it happens after the read-back, and the read-back already matched the manual. Then you sent open hand and the count one through five, then point-at-me and handshake. My reading: the step is Blind counting the five wires aloud, touching each wire in order while speaking its number. Final confirmations, thumbs up or thumbs down, fist between answers, open hand with finger counts to explain anything else. Question one: thumbs up if the step is exactly that Blind touches wire one and says one, wire two and says two, wire three and says three, wire four and says four, wire five and says five. Question two: thumbs up if after that count Blind still waits for my words cut now before cutting wire four; thumbs down if Blind cuts wire four immediately after finishing the count. Question three: thumbs up if something must be done after cutting wire four; thumbs down if cutting wire four alone ends it. Question four: thumbs up if your answers plus this step are the complete rule and nothing else remains; thumbs down if something is still missing, and then open hand with counts saying how many things.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your answers arrived: yes, you spoke the read-back, and no, there is nothing else to feel on the bomb. That second answer matters: Mute says the one missing step before the cut is something you speak aloud. My working reading, now awaiting Mute's final confirmation: you count the five wires aloud. Memorise this script. When you hear my message that begins with the words cut now, you will do exactly this: touch the first wire from the left and say the word one, move to the second and say two, third and say three, fourth and say four, fifth and say five. Then say aloud: wire four, the green wire, cutting now. Then cut wire four and nothing else. If my message begins with the word hold instead, stand by and touch nothing. Until one of those messages arrives, your hands stay completely off the bomb. Next round I expect Mute's verdict, and the round after you either hear cut now with this script, or hold.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[white] 3:[purple] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👍 ✊ 👎 ✊ 👍]

Mute's verdict is in, and it's a clean green light: **Q1 yes** — the step is exactly Blind touching each wire in order while speaking its number; **Q2 yes** — Blind still waits for my "cut now" after the count; **Q3 no** — nothing follows the cut; **Q4 yes** — the rule is now complete, nothing else remains. Blind's 👍 confirms the script is memorised and they're standing by.

Every layer has now been triple-checked: the wire's identity (fourth from left = green, confirmed by Mute against my colour report, anchored by the shared display-facing hold), the rule's conditions (display six, yellow light — both still true on my board this very round), the pre-cut step (spoken wire count, after the verified read-back), and completeness (the manual-holder's explicit yes). The one contradiction that ever appeared was caught by my forced-choice protocol and retracted by Mute themselves; every answer since has been consistent across three rounds. Nothing is left to verify that questions can reach. The bomb has sat frozen at six the whole game, but I've spent enough rounds — it's time to spend the answer instead. This round I authorise the cut.

